grades.quote: PTE_R controls whether instructions are allowed to read to the page. PTE_W controls whether instructions are allowed to write to the page. PTE_X controls whether the CPU may interpret the content of the page as instructions and execute them. PTE_U controls whether instructions in user mode are allowed to access the page; if PTE_U is not set, the PTE can be used only in supervisor mode.
grades.reason: Directly explains each PTE flag: R allows reads, W allows writes, X allows execution, and U allows user-mode access (supervisor-only if U is clear). It also covers V and page faults.

grades.quote: The permission bits, R, W, and X, indicate whether the page is readable, writable, and executable, respectively. When all three are zero, the PTE is a pointer to the next level of the page table; otherwise, it is a leaf PTE. Writable pages must also be marked readable; the contrary combinations are reserved for future use.
grades.reason: Gives the RISC-V Sv32 meaning of R, W and X. It covers the all-zero pointer case and the rule that writable pages must be readable. The quoted text does not explain the U bit.

grades.quote: When MXR=0, only loads from pages marked readable (R=1 in Figure 67) will succeed. When MXR=1, loads from pages marked either readable or executable (R=1 or X=1) will succeed.
grades.reason: Describes how sstatus MXR and SUM modify the effect of the R, X and U bits. MXR lets loads succeed on executable pages, and SUM governs S-mode access to U pages. It also says S-mode can never execute from user pages. This is useful interaction detail but does not define the bits themselves.
Covers physical memory attributes and PMA checking. It does not explain the R/W/X/U page-table-entry permission bits.
